mainTopic: The sources for the scope of אחות אשתו and אשת אח, the extra punishments written for specific עריות, and when הַעֲרָאָה counts as a forbidden act.
overview: The גמרא notes that our משנה forbids a wife's sister whether she shares a father or a mother with the wife. After weighing a comparison to אחותו against one to דודתו, it learns the rule from אשת אח, which matches on both points. A ברייתא then proves that אשת אח itself applies to a brother from either parent: two logical comparisons cancel out, so the extra words ״עֶרְוַת אָחִיךָ הִיא״ decide it. The גמרא defends that reading against attempts to use those words for other cases. It also learns from the word ״הִיא״ that a maternal brother's wife stays forbidden even after her husband dies. Next it explains why the תורה spells out כרת for a sister, and ״עֲרִירִים״ for an aunt. Last, it asks where we learn that הַעֲרָאָה, the first stage of relations, counts for ordinary לאוין and for the לאוין of כהונה. The source for prohibitions that come from an עשה is asked at the end and answered on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The משנה implies a wife's sister is forbidden from either parent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה that אחות אשתו is forbidden whether she shares a father or a mother with the wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see from here that a wife's sister, whether from the father or from the mother, is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what our משנה implies: a wife's sister is forbidden even if she and the wife share only a mother. This sets up the question about where that comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלמא means the גמרא is drawing an inference, not quoting a direct statement. The point that needs a source is the mother's side, since the פסוק just says 'her sister' without giving details.

keyTerms.meaning: So we see / apparently (introduces an inference)
His wife's sister

keyTerms.term: בֵּין מִן הָאָב בֵּין מִן הָאֵם
keyTerms.meaning: Whether from the father or from the mother
Forbidden

phrases.english: Apparently, his wife's sister,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מִן הָאָב בֵּין מִן הָאֵם — אֲסוּרוֹת.
phrases.english: whether from the father or from the mother, is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by drawing an inference from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אחות אשתו is forbidden whether she shares a father or a mother with the wife.

steps.title: Asking for the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the איסור covers a wife's sister from either parent.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule it just inferred. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not whether אחות אשתו is forbidden at all, since the תורה says that openly. It is about the wider scope, so that a sister through the mother is included too.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it? (short for מְנָא לַן)

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the 'from the mother too' part, not the basic איסור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule inferred in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that the איסור of אחות אשתו covers a sister from the mother as well.

steps.title: Learned from one's own sister
steps.stepSummary: The rule is learned from אחותו: just as one's own sister is forbidden from either parent, so is a wife's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from his sister. Just as his sister is forbidden whether from the father or from the mother, so too here, whether from the father or from the mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we compare a wife's sister to a man's own sister. A man's own sister is forbidden from both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says openly that one's own sister is forbidden whether she is 'his father's daughter or his mother's daughter.' The גמרא carries that two-sided scope over to אחות אשתו.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns / derives
His (own) sister
So too here

phrases.english: He derives it from his sister.

phrases.aramaic: מָה אֲחוֹתוֹ — בֵּין מִן הָאָב בֵּין מִן הָאֵם,
phrases.english: Just as his sister is forbidden whether from the father or from the mother,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן — בֵּין מִן הָאָב בֵּין מִן הָאֵם.
phrases.english: so too here, whether from the father or from the mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Compare to אחותו, which is forbidden from both the father's side and the mother's side.

steps.title: Why not learn from the aunt instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: learn instead from דודתו, which applies only on the father's side. Then a wife's sister would be forbidden only from the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him learn from his aunt: just as his aunt is forbidden from the father but not from the mother, so too here, from the father but not from the mother!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison by offering a different one, to דודתו, his uncle's wife. That comparison would give the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איסור of דודתו covers only the wife of his father's brother through the father, not through the mother. If אחות אשתו were compared to her, the mother's-side sister would be permitted. So the גמרא needs a reason to prefer one comparison over the other.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him learn (a suggestion that works as a challenge)
His aunt (here: his uncle's wife)
But not from the mother

steps.confusionAlert: Here דודתו is the wife of his father's brother, an aunt through marriage. Her איסור applies only when the uncle is the father's brother through the father.

phrases.english: But let him derive it from his aunt:
phrases.notes: This is the wife of his father's brother.

phrases.aramaic: מָה דּוֹדָתוֹ מִן הָאָב וְלֹא מִן הָאֵם,
phrases.english: just as his aunt is forbidden from the father and not from the mother,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן מִן הָאָב וְלֹא מִן הָאֵם!
phrases.english: so too here, from the father and not from the mother!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison of step 3 with a competing comparison.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of אחות אשתו to אחותו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A competing comparison to דודתו is just as available and would limit the איסור to the father's side.

steps.title: His own relatives fit better
steps.stepSummary: Learning from אחותו makes more sense because both are relatives of himself, while דודתו is forbidden as his father's relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is reasonable that he should learn from his sister, since that learns his own relatives from his own relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the first comparison. A wife's sister and one's own sister are both counted as his own relatives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison is stronger when the two cases share a key feature. אחות אשתו and אחותו are both relatives connected to him directly. דודתו is forbidden because of his father.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable / it makes sense
He should have learned
His own relatives

phrases.english: It is reasonable that he should derive it from his sister,
since that derives his own relatives from his own relatives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Prefers one comparison because the cases share a feature.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One could learn from דודתו and limit the איסור to the father's side.
steps.terutzMaskana: אחותו is the better match, since both are his own relatives.

steps.title: On the contrary: the aunt matches through marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: דודתו is a better match, since both she and אחות אשתו are forbidden only because of a marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, he should learn from his aunt, since that learns a matter caused by קידושין from a matter caused by קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא argues the opposite way: the aunt comparison is stronger. Like a wife's sister, she is forbidden only because of a marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man's own sister is forbidden by blood. A wife's sister is forbidden only because he married the wife, and the uncle's wife is forbidden only because the uncle married her. So each comparison has a point in its favor, and neither wins clearly.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
Through קידושין (a marriage)
A matter / case

phrases.english: On the contrary, he should derive it from his aunt,
since that derives a matter forbidden through betrothal
from a matter forbidden through betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 5 around by pointing to a competing shared feature.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 5 that אחותו is the better match.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דודתו shares a different, equally strong feature: both איסורים come about only through קידושין.

steps.title: The answer: learn from a brother's wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns instead from אשת אח, which matches on both points: it comes through קידושין, and it involves his own relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we learn from a brother's wife, since it is both a matter caused by קידושין and his own relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the argument with a third source, אשת אח. It shares both features at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A brother's wife is forbidden only because the brother married her, which matches the aunt. She is also tied to him through his own brother, which matches his sister. With both features, she is the best match, and the two-sided rule carries over to אחות אשתו.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a new solution)
A brother's wife
We learn / derive

steps.whatToRemember: When two comparisons each have one point in their favor, the גמרא looks for a source that has both. Here that source is אשת אח.

phrases.english: Rather, we derive it from a brother's wife,
since it is a matter forbidden through betrothal,
and his own relatives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the standoff between steps 5 and 6 by choosing a source that has both features.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אחות אשתו is forbidden from either parent, learned from אשת אח, which shares both the marriage feature and the own-relatives feature.

steps.title: How do we know a brother's wife applies on both sides?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that אשת אח itself is forbidden whether the brother shares a father or a mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a brother's wife itself, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that everything rests on אשת אח, the גמרא asks how we know her איסור covers both kinds of brothers. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison only works if אשת אח truly applies from both the father and the mother. Otherwise it could not pass that wider scope on to אחות אשתו.

keyTerms.meaning: Itself

phrases.english: And a brother's wife itself, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: He's asking how we know it covers a brother from the mother too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks the basis of the source chosen in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that אשת אח applies whether the brother shares a father or a mother.

steps.title: A ברייתא on the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the פסוק about a brother's wife applies whether he is a brother from the father or from the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: 'The nakedness of your brother's wife you shall not uncover,' whether from the father or from the mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. It reads the פסוק about אשת אח as covering both a father's-side brother and a mother's-side brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only opens the ברייתא and states its claim. The ברייתא has not proven it yet. In the next steps it tests two logical comparisons, and only in step 15 does it find the real source, the extra words ״עֶרְוַת אָחִיךָ הִיא״.

keyTerms.meaning: The nakedness of (a forbidden relationship)
You shall not uncover

steps.whatToRemember: The chain is: אשת אח applies on both sides (from the פסוק) → אחות אשתו is learned from it → a wife's sister is forbidden whether from the father or the mother.

phrases.english: As it is taught: "You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother's wife,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:16

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מִן הָאָב בֵּין מִן הָאֵם.
phrases.english: whether from the father or from the mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא עֶרְוַת אֵשֶׁת אָחִיךָ לֹא תְגַלֵּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא teaches that the איסור of 'ערות אשת אחיך' covers a brother from either the father or the mother. The ברייתא goes on to prove this, and the proof in step 15 comes from the words 'ערות אחיך היא'.

steps.title: Does a brother's wife include a brother from the mother?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the איסור of אשת אח covers a brother from the father and also a brother from the mother, or only a brother from the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it applies whether the brother is from the father or from the mother? Or maybe it applies only to a brother from the father, and not to one from the mother?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא opens by setting up the question it is going to work through. It lays out two possible readings of the איסור of a brother's wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A brother can share only a father with him, only a mother, or both. The ברייתא wants to know if a brother who shares only a mother also makes his wife forbidden. This question sets up the whole back-and-forth that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: "Do you say": a ברייתא formula that opens a question about how to read a law
From the father: a brother who has the same father
From the mother: a brother who has the same mother

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בֵּין מִן הָאָב בֵּין מִן הָאֵם,
phrases.english: Do you say whether from the father or from the mother,
or is it only from the father
and not from the mother?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בֵּין מִן הָאָב בֵּין מִן הָאֵם, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִן הָאָב וְלֹא מִן הָאֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא that began in Step 9 by asking whether its opening claim is correct.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the איסור of אשת אח apply to a maternal brother's wife too, or only to a paternal brother's wife?

steps.title: Logic: compare to his sister
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא tries to learn by logic from אחותו, which is forbidden whether she shares his father or his mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is logical: the תורה made him liable here, and it made him liable for his sister. Just as with his sister it applies whether she is from the father or the mother, so too here it applies whether the brother is from the father or the mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא offers a first answer by comparing a brother's wife to one's own sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אשת אח and אחותו carry a punishment, so the ברייתא compares them. Since אחותו is forbidden from either parent, אשת אח should be too. This is the same kind of comparison to אחותו that the גמרא made in Step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is logical": the ברייתא tries to prove the law by reasoning
Liable to punishment
His sister

phrases.english: And it is logical:
He is liable here, and he is liable for his sister.
phrases.notes: "Here" means a brother's wife.

phrases.aramaic: מָה אֲחוֹתוֹ — בֵּין מִן הָאָב בֵּין מִן הָאֵם,
phrases.english: Just as his sister: whether from the father or from the mother,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן — בֵּין מִן הָאָב בֵּין מִן הָאֵם.
phrases.english: so too here: whether from the father or from the mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִין הוּא: חַיָּיב כָּאן, וְחַיָּיב בַּאֲחוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first logical answer to the question in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: אשת אח applies to both a paternal and a maternal brother
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to אחותו, which is forbidden from either parent

steps.title: Or compare to his aunt instead
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a different comparison, to דודתו, which leads to the opposite answer: paternal only.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or go this way: he is liable here, and he is liable for his aunt. Just as with his aunt it applies only from the father and not from the mother, so too here it should apply only from the father and not from the mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on Step 11 by offering a competing comparison that points the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דודתו here is the wife of his father's brother, and that איסור only applies when the uncle is the father's brother from the father. If אשת אח is compared to her instead, it would be limited to a paternal brother. Now there are two comparisons that give opposite results.

keyTerms.meaning: "Go this way": suggests a different comparison
His aunt: here, the wife of his father's brother

phrases.english: Or go this way:
he is liable here and he is liable for his aunt,

phrases.aramaic: מָה דּוֹדָתוֹ — מִן הָאָב וְלֹא מִן הָאֵם,
phrases.english: just as his aunt: from the father and not from the mother,
phrases.notes: He means the uncle must be his father's brother from the father, not from the mother.

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן — מִן הָאָב וְלֹא מִן הָאֵם?!
phrases.english: so too here: from the father and not from the mother?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ כְּלָךְ לְדֶרֶךְ זוֹ: חַיָּיב כָּאן וְחַיָּיב בְּדוֹדָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 11 with a competing comparison.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison to אחותו in Step 11
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דודתו is also a punishable איסור, and it applies to the father's side only, so it could just as easily be the model.

steps.title: His sister is closer: both are his own relatives
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא argues that אחותו is the better match, since both she and his brother's wife come through his own relatives, while דודתו comes through his father's relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us see which it is more similar to. We learn his own relatives from his own relatives, and his aunt cannot prove otherwise, because she is a relative of his father.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא weighs the two comparisons and defends the one to אחותו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His brother and his sister are both his own direct relatives. דודתו is connected to him only through his father. So the ברייתא says we should learn from the closer case, which is אחותו.

keyTerms.meaning: "Let us see which it resembles": weighing two comparisons
His own relatives
"Cannot prove": this case is not a good model

phrases.english: Let us see which it is similar to:
we learn his own relatives from his own relatives,
phrases.notes: His brother's wife is learned from his sister. Both come through his own siblings.

phrases.english: and his aunt cannot prove otherwise, since she is among the father's relatives.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִרְאֶה לְמִי דּוֹמֶה: דָּנִין קְרוֹבֵי עַצְמוֹ מִקְּרוֹבֵי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 by defending the comparison to אחותו.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: דודתו is just as good a model as אחותו
steps.terutzMaskana: אחותו is closer because both cases involve his own relatives

steps.title: His aunt is closer: both come through marriage
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא pushes back: דודתו matches better, since both she and a brother's wife are forbidden only through קידושין, while אחותו is forbidden by birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or go this way: we learn a case that comes through betrothal from a case that comes through betrothal, and his sister cannot prove otherwise, because hers is a prohibition that comes on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges Step 13 with a different point of similarity that favors דודתו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A brother's wife and an uncle's wife are both forbidden only because someone married them. A sister is forbidden from birth, with no marriage needed. By this measure דודתו is the better model, so the ברייתא is now stuck between two equal arguments.

keyTerms.meaning: Through betrothal: forbidden only because of a marriage
A prohibition that comes on its own, from birth, with no marriage needed

phrases.english: Or go this way:
we learn a matter that comes through betrothal,
from a matter that comes through betrothal,
and his sister cannot prove otherwise,
since hers is a prohibition that comes on its own.
phrases.notes: She is forbidden just by being born his sister. Nobody had to marry anyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ כְּלָךְ לְדֶרֶךְ זוֹ: דָּנִין דָּבָר שֶׁעַל יְדֵי קִדּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 13 with a competing point of similarity.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 13 that אחותו is the closer match
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both אשת אח and דודתו come from קידושין, so דודתו is just as close, or closer.

steps.title: The פסוק settles it: both kinds of brother
steps.stepSummary: Since logic cannot decide, the ברייתא learns from the extra words ״עֶרְוַת אָחִיךָ הִיא״ that the איסור applies whether the brother shares a father or a mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "It is your brother's nakedness." This teaches that it applies whether he is a brother from the father or from the mother.
steps.whatsHappening: Neither comparison won, so the ברייתא turns to the פסוק itself to give the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each comparison had a good point in its favor, so logic ended in a tie. The extra words ״עֶרְוַת אָחִיךָ הִיא״ teach that any brother counts, whether from the father or from the mother. This is the source the גמרא asked for in Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: "The verse says": introduces the פסוק that decides the question
"It is your brother's nakedness" (ויקרא 18:16)

steps.whatToRemember: When two logical comparisons cancel each other out, the ברייתא relies on the פסוק. ״עֶרְוַת אָחִיךָ הִיא״ teaches that אשת אח is forbidden whether the brother shares a father or a mother.

phrases.english: The verse states: "It is your brother's nakedness,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:16

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מִן הָאָב בֵּין מִן הָאֵם.
phrases.english: whether from the father or from the mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the logical tie between Steps 13 and 14 by bringing a פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אשת אח is forbidden whether the brother is from the father or from the mother, learned from ״עֶרְוַת אָחִיךָ הִיא״.

steps.title: Maybe both halves of the verse are about a paternal brother's wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that both halves of the פסוק refer to a paternal brother's wife. One half would forbid her when she has children, and the other would forbid her when she has no children, both during her husband's lifetime.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that both parts of the פסוק talk about the wife of a paternal brother. One part is about a woman who has children, during her husband's lifetime. The other part is about a woman who has no children, during her husband's lifetime.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's reading of the extra words. It says the extra words could be teaching a different case about a paternal brother, not about a maternal brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used the extra half of the פסוק to add the maternal brother. The גמרא points out that the extra half could instead split the paternal-brother case into two situations, with children and without children. If that is right, there is no source left for the maternal brother.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one, meaning both halves of the פסוק
The wife of a brother who shares his father
During her husband's lifetime, for example after a divorce
She has children from her husband

phrases.english: But say that both this and that
phrases.notes: He means both halves of the פסוק: ״עֶרְוַת אֵשֶׁת אָחִיךָ״ and ״עֶרְוַת אָחִיךָ הִיא״ (ויקרא 18:16).

phrases.english: refer to the wife of a paternal brother,
one is about a woman who has children
during her husband's lifetime,
and one is about a woman who has no children
during her husband's lifetime!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בְּאֵשֶׁת אָח מִן הָאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 15, which used the extra words for the maternal brother
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of ״עֶרְוַת אָחִיךָ הִיא״ to include a maternal brother
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra words could be used up on a different paternal-brother case, with children versus without children during the husband's lifetime, so they would not teach anything about a maternal brother.

steps.title: The childless case during the husband's life is already known from רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a childless woman being forbidden during her husband's lifetime is already learned from רב הונא, so the extra words are not needed for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of a woman without children during her husband's lifetime is already learned from רב הונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. That case already has its own source, so the extra words are still free to teach about the maternal brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק is not used to teach something we already know from another source. Since רב הונא already gave a source for the childless woman during her husband's lifetime, the extra words cannot be used up on that case.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes out from, meaning it is learned from

phrases.english: A woman with no children, during her husband's lifetime,
is learned from רב הונא.
phrases.notes: This points back to רב הונא's teaching on the previous עמוד (54b).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לָהּ בָּנִים בְּחַיֵּי בַּעְלָהּ מִדְּרַב הוּנָא נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: The case already has another source, so the extra words are not needed for it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra words might teach that a childless paternal brother's wife is forbidden during her husband's lifetime
steps.terutzMaskana: That case is already learned from רב הונא, so the extra words remain available for the maternal brother

steps.title: Maybe the halves cover a woman with children before and after her husband's death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a new split. Both halves are about a paternal brother's wife who has children: one half forbids her during her husband's lifetime, and the other forbids her after his death.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that both parts of the פסוק talk about the wife of a paternal brother. One part is about a woman with children during her husband's lifetime. The other part is about a woman with children after her husband's death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a second attempt to use up the extra words on a paternal-brother case, this time dividing by before and after the husband's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first split failed because רב הונא already covered the childless case. So the גמרא now splits differently, into a woman with children during her husband's life and a woman with children after he dies. If this works, there is again no source for the maternal brother.

keyTerms.meaning: After her husband's death

phrases.english: But say that both this and that
refer to the wife of a paternal brother,
one is about a woman who has children
during her husband's lifetime,
and one is about a woman who has children
after her husband's death!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בְּאֵשֶׁת אָח מִן הָאָב, חֲדָא דְּיֵשׁ לָהּ בָּנִים בְּחַיֵּי בַּעְלָהּ, וַחֲדָא דְּיֵשׁ לָהּ בָּנִים לְאַחַר מִיתַת בַּעְלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 17 turned away the first split, this step offers a second way to use up the extra words
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of the extra words for a maternal brother
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra words could teach that a paternal brother's wife who has children stays forbidden even after her husband's death, which would use them up.

steps.title: The case after death is inferred from the permission of יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that no פסוק is needed for a woman with children after her husband's death. Since the תורה permits only a childless widow to the brother, a widow with children must be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman with children after her husband's death does not need a פסוק. Since the תורה says a woman without children is permitted, it follows that a woman with children is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge. It shows that this case can be figured out from the תורה's permission of יבום, so the extra words are not needed for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה allows יבום only when the dead brother left no children. From that we infer the opposite: if there are children, she stays forbidden. Because this case can be inferred, the extra words are still free for the maternal brother.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not need a פסוק
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
This implies, introducing an inference from the opposite case

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לָהּ בָּנִים לְאַחַר מִיתַת בַּעְלָהּ
phrases.english: A woman who has children, after her husband's death,
does not need a פסוק,
since the Torah says
phrases.notes: This is the מצוה of יבום, where the brother marries his brother's childless widow (דברים 25:5).

phrases.english: that a woman who has no children is permitted,
this implies that if she has children, she is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ לָהּ בָּנִים לְאַחַר מִיתַת בַּעְלָהּ לָא צְרִיכָא קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: The case is inferred from another פסוק by reasoning from the opposite case, so no extra words are needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra words might teach that a widow with children is forbidden to her husband's brother
steps.terutzMaskana: That is already implied by the יבום permission being limited to a childless widow

steps.title: The יבום permission might imply something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference from step 19. Maybe the difference between a childless widow and a widow with children is not forbidden versus permitted. It could be about marrying others, or about מצוה versus רשות. If so, the extra words are needed to forbid the widow with children.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps a woman without children is forbidden to everyone else and permitted to the יבם, while a woman with children is permitted to everyone and also permitted to the יבם. Or perhaps for a woman without children marrying her is a מצוה, and for a woman with children it is optional.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of step 19. It shows that the תורה's permission of a childless widow does not have to mean that a widow with children is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 assumed the opposite of 'childless means permitted' is 'with children means forbidden.' The גמרא offers two other ways to read the contrast. One is that the difference is only whether she may marry other men. The other is that the difference is a מצוה versus a choice. Either way, the widow with children might still be permitted to the brother, so a פסוק would be needed to forbid her. That threatens to use up the extra words again.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
To everyone, meaning to other men in general
She is permitted
The dead husband's brother who may do יבום
Alternatively
Optional, a permitted choice rather than a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: The two 'perhaps' readings are not two separate questions. They are two different ways the גמרא shows that 'childless is permitted' does not have to imply 'with children is forbidden.'

phrases.aramaic: וְדִלְמָא: אֵין לָהּ בָּנִים אֲסוּרָה לְעָלְמָא
phrases.english: But perhaps a woman with no children is forbidden to everyone else
and permitted to the יבם,
while a woman with children is permitted to everyone
and also permitted to the יבם!

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: אֵין לָהּ בָּנִים מִצְוָה,
phrases.english: Alternatively: a woman with no children is a מצוה,
phrases.notes: He means it is a מצוה for the brother to marry her.

phrases.english: while a woman with children is optional!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא: אֵין לָהּ בָּנִים אֲסוּרָה לְעָלְמָא וְשַׁרְיָא לְיָבָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference used in step 19, bringing back the challenge of step 18
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that a widow with children is forbidden to her husband's brother
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The contrast with the childless widow could be about marrying others, or about מצוה versus רשות, rather than forbidden versus permitted to the brother
steps.whyThisMatters: If the inference fails, the widow with children needs her own פסוק. That would use up the extra words, and the ברייתא's source for the maternal brother would be in doubt again.

steps.title: Maybe the widow with children is forbidden only by a weak prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds another way the inference from step 19 could fail. Even if a widow with children is forbidden, the איסור would come only from the positive מצוה of יבום, so it would be a weak לאו הבא מכלל עשה. Then the extra words would be needed to make it a full איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: if she has no children, yes, she is permitted. If she has children, no, she is not. But a prohibition that only comes out of a positive command counts only as a positive command!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to reject the proof from step 19. Even if a widow with children is forbidden, that איסור could be too weak without the extra words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said the difference between the two widows might not be forbidden versus permitted at all. Here the גמרא says: even if it is forbidden, that "no" is only inferred from the עשה of יבום. A prohibition learned that way has only the strength of an עשה, with no כרת, so the extra words would still be needed to give the full איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively; another way to say it
A prohibition that is only inferred from a positive command
A positive command; here, a weaker level of prohibition with no כרת

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the widow with children is permitted. It is saying that, without the extra words, her איסור might only be a weak one with no כרת.

phrases.english: Alternatively,
if she has no children, yes, she is permitted to the brother,
if she has children, no, she is not permitted,
but a prohibition that comes out of a positive command has only the status of a positive command!
phrases.notes: So that "no" would carry no כרת, which is why the extra words would still be needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: אֵין לָהּ בָּנִים — אִין, יֵשׁ לָהּ בָּנִים — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second reason to the rejection in step 20 of the inference made in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim in step 19 that no פסוק is needed to forbid a widow with children.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An איסור inferred from the עשה of יבום would only be a weak לאו הבא מכלל עשה, so a פסוק would still be needed to make it a full איסור with כרת.

steps.title: Another verse already teaches the full prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a different פסוק, "ערות אחיו גלה", already teaches the full איסור of a brother's wife. So the extra words in the first פסוק are free to teach something else: the wife of a maternal brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה wrote another verse: "He has uncovered his brother's nakedness."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of steps 20 and 21 by pointing to another פסוק that already gives the full איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that the extra words were needed to make the איסור of a widow with children a full one. But "ערות אחיו גלה" already teaches that, with כרת. So the extra words are not needed for this case, and the ברייתא can use them to include a maternal brother's wife.

keyTerms.meaning: Another verse
"He has uncovered his brother's nakedness"

steps.whatToRemember: The full איסור of a brother's wife comes from "ערות אחיו גלה", so the extra words in the first פסוק teach about a maternal brother's wife.

phrases.english: The Torah wrote another verse:
"He has uncovered his brother's nakedness."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:21

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in steps 20 and 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Another source already covers the case, so the extra words are free for a new teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra words were needed to make the איסור of a widow with children a full איסור.
steps.terutzMaskana: "ערות אחיו גלה" teaches the full איסור, so the extra words teach about a maternal brother's wife.

steps.title: Should a maternal brother's wife be permitted after his death?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: maybe a maternal brother's wife should follow the same rule as a paternal brother's wife. Since a paternal brother's wife is permitted after her husband's death through יבום, the maternal one should be permitted too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the wife of a maternal brother is like the wife of a paternal brother. Just as the wife of a paternal brother is permitted after her husband's death, so too the wife of a maternal brother should be permitted after her husband's death!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that a maternal brother's wife is included in the איסור, the גמרא asks whether she should also share the paternal brother's wife's permission after the husband dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both kinds of brother's wife come from the same פסוק, it seems they should share every rule. A paternal brother's wife can be permitted after her husband's death through יבום, so the גמרא asks why a maternal brother's wife should be any different.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of a brother from the same mother only
The wife of a brother from the same father
She is permitted

phrases.english: But say the wife of a maternal brother
is like the wife of a paternal brother:
just as the wife of a paternal brother
is permitted after her husband's death,
so too the wife of a maternal brother
should be permitted after her husband's death!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא אֵשֶׁת אָח מִן הָאֵם כְּאֵשֶׁת אָח מִן הָאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inclusion of a maternal brother's wife that was just established in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a maternal brother's wife is forbidden, including after her husband's death.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she is learned from the same פסוק as a paternal brother's wife, she should share the permission after the husband's death.

steps.title: The word "היא" keeps her forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from the word "היא" in the פסוק: she stays as she was. A maternal brother's wife remains forbidden after her husband's death, just as she was during his life.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says "she": she shall remain as she is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 23 with one word from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "היא" ("she is your brother's nakedness") teaches that her forbidden status does not change. So a maternal brother's wife stays forbidden even after her husband dies, and only a paternal brother's wife can become permitted through יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: "She"; here it teaches that her status stays the same
She shall remain as she is

steps.whatToRemember: A maternal brother's wife is forbidden both during the husband's life and after his death, because of the word "היא".

phrases.english: The verse says "she,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:16: "she is your brother's nakedness."

phrases.english: she shall remain as she is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A word in the פסוק limits the permission.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A maternal brother's wife should be permitted after her husband's death, like a paternal brother's wife.
steps.terutzMaskana: "היא" teaches that she stays forbidden after her husband's death.

steps.title: Why is כרת written separately for one's sister?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic. Since one general פסוק already gives כרת for all the עריות, why does the תורה write כרת separately for one's sister?
steps.simpleTranslation: One's sister, where כרת is written about her: why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question. It is setting up a search for what the separate mention of כרת for a sister comes to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the עריות are grouped together, and one פסוק already gives כרת for all of them. So writing כרת again for a sister seems extra. The גמרא assumes it must be there to teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: One's sister
Being cut off; the punishment for the עריות
Why do I need it?

phrases.english: One's sister, where כרת is written about her,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:29 already gives כרת for all the עריות, so the separate mention for a sister (ויקרא 20:17) looks extra.

phrases.english: why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחוֹתוֹ דִּכְתַב בָּהּ כָּרֵת לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the brother's wife ends.
steps.kashyaTarget: The separate mention of כרת for one's sister.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general פסוק already gives כרת for all the עריות, so repeating it for a sister seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The sister's separate כרת teaches liability for each forbidden relation
steps.stepSummary: The separate mention of כרת for a sister teaches רבי יוחנן's rule: a person who violates all the עריות in one lapse of awareness is liable for each one separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for רבי יוחנן's teaching. רבי יוחנן said: if a person committed all of them in one lapse of awareness, he is liable for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 25. The תורה singles out the sister's כרת to teach that each forbidden relation counts as its own separate sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this פסוק, we might think all the עריות are one big איסור, so someone who sinned many times in one forgetful state would bring only one קרבן. Singling out the sister shows that each ערוה stands on its own. So a person who sinned with many עריות in one lapse of awareness owes a separate קרבן for each.

keyTerms.meaning: One lapse of awareness: the person forgot or did not know the איסור the whole time, without remembering in between
Liable for each and every one; each act counts as a separate sin
Being 'cut off', a heavenly punishment for very serious sins

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule that each ערוה is its own separate איסור. It matters for how many קרבנות חטאת a person must bring.

phrases.english: For that of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
phrases.notes: This answers step 25: the sister's separate כרת is needed for רבי יוחנן's rule.

phrases.english: as Rabbi Yoḥanan said
that if he committed all of them
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all the different forbidden relations.

phrases.english: in one lapse of awareness
he is liable for each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25 about why the sister's כרת is written separately.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the seemingly extra פסוק a new teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The separate כרת for a sister seems unnecessary, since the general פסוק already covers it.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that each ערוה is a separate איסור, so one is liable for each even within one lapse of awareness.

steps.title: How does רבי יצחק learn that each ערוה is separate?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק uses the sister's separate כרת to teach that the punishment is כרת and not מלקות. So where does he learn that each ערוה counts separately?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יצחק, who said: all those liable to כרת were included in the general rule, so why was כרת singled out for one's sister? To judge him with כרת and not with מלקות. Then where do we learn to divide them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 26 using רבי יצחק's view. He already uses the sister's פסוק for a different lesson, so it cannot also teach רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יצחק, the sister's פסוק teaches that this sinner gets כרת instead of lashes. That uses up the פסוק. So the גמרא asks what source he has for 'dividing', meaning treating each ערוה as a separate sin.

keyTerms.meaning: They were included in the general rule
Was taken out, singled out from the general rule
Lashes, the usual punishment for breaking a לא תעשה
To divide; to treat each ערוה as a separate sin

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יצחק does not argue with רבי יוחנן's rule. He agrees that each ערוה is separate. He just needs a different פסוק to teach it.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yitzḥak, who said:
all who are liable to karet were included in the general rule,
phrases.notes: This is the general פסוק from step 25 that gives כרת to all the עריות.

phrases.english: and why was karet singled out for his sister?
To judge him with karet and not with lashes.
To divide, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in step 26 according to a different אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of the sister's פסוק as the source for רבי יוחנן's rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יצחק already uses that פסוק to teach כרת instead of מלקות, so it cannot also teach dividing. He needs another source.

steps.title: רבי יצחק learns it from the פסוק about a נדה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק learns that each ערוה counts separately from the פסוק 'and to a woman in the separation of her impurity', which makes a person liable for each woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: He derives it from 'And to a woman in the separation of her impurity': to make him liable for each and every woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 27. רבי יצחק has a different source: the פסוק about not approaching a נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אשה' (a woman) in the נדה פסוק is read as teaching liability for each woman separately. This gives רבי יצחק the rule of dividing without needing the sister's פסוק, which stays free for his own lesson about כרת instead of lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it, he learns it out
A woman in her time of menstrual impurity
Each and every woman

phrases.english: He derives it
from "And to a woman in the separation of her impurity,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:19

phrases.english: to make him liable for each and every woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִ״וְּאֶל אִשָּׁה בְּנִדַּת טוּמְאָתָהּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27 by giving רבי יצחק a different source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Provides an alternative פסוק as the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יצחק seems to have no source for treating each ערוה separately.
steps.terutzMaskana: He learns it from the נדה פסוק, which makes a person liable for each woman.

steps.title: Why does the תורה write 'childless' about an aunt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תורה adds the punishment 'they shall be childless' for relations with one's aunt.
steps.simpleTranslation: His aunt, about whom the Merciful One wrote 'they shall be childless': why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the same pattern and asks about another punishment the Torah spells out. It wants to know why the 'childless' punishment is written for an aunt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the עריות already carry כרת from the general פסוק. So writing a special 'childless' punishment for this case seems unnecessary, and the גמרא asks what it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: His aunt
Childless
Why do I need it? A question about a seemingly extra phrase

phrases.english: His aunt, about whom the Merciful One wrote
"they shall be childless," why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: דּוֹדָתוֹ דִּכְתַב בַּהּ רַחֲמָנָא ״עֲרִירִים יִהְיוּ״, לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same 'why is this written separately' question from step 25 to a different punishment.
steps.kashyaTarget: The extra 'childless' phrase written for an aunt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general פסוק already gives כרת to all the עריות, so a separate punishment phrase seems extra.

steps.title: רבה reconciles two 'childless' פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: The phrase is needed for רבה's teaching. One פסוק says 'they shall be childless' and another says 'they shall die childless'. If he has children, he buries them. If he has none, he stays childless.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for רבה's teaching. רבה pointed out a contradiction: it is written 'they shall be childless,' and it is written 'they shall die childless.' How is this? If he has children, he buries them. If he has no children, he goes childless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 29 with רבה's teaching. The two different 'childless' phrases each cover a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה noticed two different wordings of the 'childless' punishment. They are not a contradiction: for a man who already has children, the punishment is that he will bury them; for a man with no children, the punishment is that he will never have any. So the extra phrase is not wasted. Together the two wordings teach both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: He pointed out a contradiction between two sources
How is this? How can both be true?
He buries them
He goes childless, he stays without children

steps.whatToRemember: The תורה's separate punishments for specific עריות each teach something new: the sister's כרת teaches that each ערוה is separate (or, for רבי יצחק, כרת instead of lashes), and the 'childless' phrases teach both cases: burying existing children, or never having children.

phrases.english: For that of Rabba.
For Rabba pointed out a contradiction:
it is written: "they shall be childless,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:21

phrases.english: and it is written: "they shall die childless,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:20

phrases.english: How is this?
If he has children, he buries them;
if he has no children, he goes childless.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29 by assigning the 'childless' phrase to רבה's teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the seemingly extra phrase a new teaching by reconciling two פסוקים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'childless' phrase seems extra, since כרת is already given for all the עריות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two wordings teach two cases: a man with children buries them, and a man without children stays childless.

steps.title: Why both childlessness phrases are needed
steps.stepSummary: Each phrase alone would cover only one group of children: those born before the sin, or those born after it. So the תורה needs both.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to write 'they shall be childless' and also 'they shall die childless'. If the תורה had written only 'they shall be childless', I would have thought it means only children he had before his sin, but not children born after. So it wrote 'they shall die childless'. And if it had written only 'they shall die childless', I would have thought it means only children born after his sin, but not the ones from before. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the תורה needed two separate phrases about childlessness. It shows that each one would have left a gap by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עֲרִירִים יִהְיוּ' alone would only cover children who already existed before the sin. 'עֲרִירִים יָמֻתוּ' alone would only cover children born after the sin. Writing both teaches that all his children are included, whether born before or after the sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Childless
It is necessary (both sources are needed, and neither is extra)
I would have said (a mistaken first thought)
His sin

steps.whatToRemember: Two phrases cover two groups of children. 'יִהְיוּ' covers those born before the sin, and 'יָמֻתוּ' covers those born after it. Together they mean he is left fully childless.

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write 'they shall be childless',
and it was necessary to write 'they shall die childless',
for if the Merciful One had written only 'they shall be childless',
I would have said: only children born up to his sin,
but those from his sin onward, no.
So the Merciful One wrote 'they shall die childless'.
And if the Merciful One had written only 'they shall die childless',
I would have said: only children from his sin onward,
but those from the beginning, no,
phrases.notes: 'From the beginning' means children he already had before the sin.

phrases.english: so both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבה's teaching from step 30 by showing that neither phrase is extra.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each source covers a case the other would miss.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One phrase alone would cover only children born before the sin, or only children born after it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both phrases are needed so that all his children are included.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the first stage of relations counts for ordinary prohibitions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that הַעֲרָאָה makes a person liable even for ordinary לאוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The initial stage of relations, for those who are liable for ordinary prohibitions: from where do we learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It asks how we know that just the first stage of relations counts as a forbidden act for ordinary לאוין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא learned that הַעֲרָאָה counts for עריות punished by death or כרת. That source does not automatically cover plain לאוין, so we need a separate source for them.

keyTerms.meaning: The first stage of relations, before the act is complete
Relationships forbidden by an ordinary negative commandment (punished by מלקות, not death or כרת)
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: The initial stage of relations for those liable for ordinary prohibitions: from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic, continuing the earlier discussion about הַעֲרָאָה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that הַעֲרָאָה makes one liable for ordinary לאוין.

steps.title: Proof from the designated maidservant
steps.stepSummary: The תורה specifically requires a complete act for שפחה חרופה. That implies that for other לאוין, הַעֲרָאָה is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Merciful One specified 'lying with seed' in the case of a designated maidservant, we can infer that for other ordinary prohibitions, one is liable even for the initial stage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the פסוק about שפחה חרופה. There the תורה says a complete act is needed. That suggests a complete act is not needed elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would the תורה stop to say 'a complete act' for this one case? Because it is an exception. So the normal rule for לאוין must be that הַעֲרָאָה already counts.

keyTerms.meaning: A maidservant designated (half-betrothed) to a man
Lying with seed, meaning a complete act of relations
By implication, we can infer

phrases.english: Since the Merciful One revealed 'lying with seed'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:20

phrases.english: regarding a designated maidservant,
we infer that those liable for ordinary prohibitions are liable for the initial stage.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּגַלִּי רַחֲמָנָא ״שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע״ גַּבֵּי שִׁפְחָה חֲרוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the תורה requires a complete act only for שפחה חרופה, the other לאוין must count even with הַעֲרָאָה.

steps.title: On the contrary: maybe ordinary prohibitions need a complete act
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the proof around. The תורה had to spell out הַעֲרָאָה for כרת cases, so maybe ordinary לאוין require a complete act.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Since the Merciful One revealed that the initial stage counts for those liable for כרת, we can infer that those liable for ordinary prohibitions are liable only for a completed act!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof by reading the פסוקים the opposite way. Maybe the special case is כרת, not שפחה חרופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה needed a special source to teach הַעֲרָאָה for חייבי כריתות. So perhaps without such a source, the default is a complete act. If so, ordinary לאוין would need גמר ביאה, and the שפחה חרופה פסוק proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
Relationships punished by כרת
Completion of the act of relations

phrases.english: On the contrary: since the Merciful One revealed
the initial stage regarding those liable for כרת,
phrases.notes: This points back to the source on the previous דף that taught הַעֲרָאָה for עריות punished by כרת.

phrases.english: we infer that those liable for ordinary prohibitions are liable only for a completed act!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference made in step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from שפחה חרופה that הַעֲרָאָה counts for ordinary לאוין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The opposite inference is just as possible: the special source for כרת cases implies that לאוין need a complete act.

steps.title: רב אשי: then the maidservant verse would be unnecessary
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that if לאוין needed a complete act anyway, the תורה would not have needed to say so for שפחה חרופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: If so, let the verse stay silent about the designated maidservant.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends the original proof. He shows that the 'on the contrary' reading would make the שפחה חרופה פסוק unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every לאו required גמר ביאה anyway, writing 'שכבת זרע' for שפחה חרופה would teach nothing new. The תורה does not waste words. So that פסוק must mark an exception, and for other לאוין הַעֲרָאָה counts.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let the verse be silent (the verse would be unnecessary)

steps.whatToRemember: For ordinary לאוין, הַעֲרָאָה makes a person liable. שפחה חרופה is the exception, where the תורה requires a complete act.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן — לִשְׁתּוֹק קְרָא מִשִּׁפְחָה חֲרוּפָה.
phrases.english: If so, let the verse be silent about the designated maidservant.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אִם כֵּן — לִשְׁתּוֹק קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'אדרבה' challenge of step 34 and restores the proof of step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the opposite reading would make a פסוק unnecessary.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Ordinary לאוין might require a complete act, since the תורה had to spell out הַעֲרָאָה for כרת cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שפחה חרופה פסוק would be unnecessary under that reading. So it is an exception, and other לאוין count with הַעֲרָאָה.

steps.title: What is the source for prohibitions special to priests?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that הַעֲרָאָה counts as a forbidden act for the לאוין that apply only to כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that the first stage of intercourse counts for those who break the prohibitions of the priesthood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new group of prohibitions, the ones only כהנים have, such as a כהן marrying a זונה. It asks for the source that הַעֲרָאָה counts for them too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in the last steps covered ordinary לאוין that apply to everyone. The לאוין of כהונה are a separate, special group that only applies to כהנים. So the גמרא will not assume they follow the general rule, and it asks for their own source.

keyTerms.meaning: Prohibitions that apply only to כהנים, such as a כהן marrying a divorcee or a זונה
Those who are liable, meaning people who break a given prohibition
From where do we know this? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: The initial stage of intercourse for those liable for the prohibitions of the priesthood, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling ordinary לאוין in steps 32-35, the גמרא extends the question to the special לאוין of כהונה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that הַעֲרָאָה counts as a forbidden act for the לאוין of כהונה.

steps.title: Learned from the word 'taking' in both places
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a גזירה שוה. The word 'taking' appears both in a כרת prohibition and in the prohibitions of כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from 'taking' and 'taking.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the same word, 'taking,' appears in the כרת prohibitions and in the כהונה prohibitions. So the rule from one group carries over to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that הַעֲרָאָה counts for כרת cases. The פסוק about a sister uses the word 'take,' and the פסוק about a כהן and a זונה also uses 'take.' Because of this shared word, a גזירה שוה moves the הַעֲרָאָה rule from כרת over to the לאוין of כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes, meaning it is derived
Taking, the verb 'to take' used in these פסוקים
A derivation that links two laws because the same word appears in both

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say 'גזירה שוה' out loud. When it repeats one word twice, like 'קִיחָה קִיחָה,' that is the signal for a גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: It is derived from 'taking' and 'taking.'
phrases.notes: One 'taking' is in ויקרא 20:17, about a sister (a כרת case). The other is ויקרא 21:7, where a כהן may not take a זונה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from the word 'taking' links the לאוין of כהונה to the כרת prohibitions, where הַעֲרָאָה already counts.

steps.title: What is the source for prohibitions that come from a positive command?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that הַעֲרָאָה counts for prohibitions that come from an עשה (a positive מצוה).
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know it for those liable for violating a positive command?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question about one more group: prohibitions that come from an עשה. The answer comes in the next section, so this line sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some marriages are forbidden only because of a positive command. One example is the first generations of Egyptian or Edomite converts, since the תורה says only the third generation may enter. This kind of prohibition is weaker than a לאו, so the גמרא needs its own source to show that הַעֲרָאָה counts here too.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who break a prohibition that comes from a positive command
A positive מצוה, a 'do' command; here a prohibition that is implied from one
The third generation, the first generation of Egyptian and Edomite converts allowed to marry into the community

phrases.english: For those liable for a positive command, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: We're still asking about הַעֲרָאָה. An example is marrying a first-generation Egyptian convert, based on דברים 23:9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having found a source for the לאוין of כהונה, the גמרא moves to the next group, prohibitions that come from an עשה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that הַעֲרָאָה counts as a forbidden act for prohibitions that come from an עשה.
